runtime_notes: Load data/municipalities.json for search suggestions.
After the user selects a municipality, load only its base GeoJSON, history GeoJSON, result profile JSON, and boundary GeoJSON.
Radar chart radii use nationwide percentile scores; labels show raw counts, national rank, and national average.
Clicking a radar axis label closes the result dialog and enables only the mapped category layers; the restore button below the result shortcut enables all 17 layers.
Profile headlines mention dining only for nationwide ranks 1-30, roads/posts and civil heritage from one item, and approximate early-modern villages from five items.
Culture cards show five items initially and can expand one card across the full card grid to reveal all stored items.
The result dialog has three pages: a Wikipedia-derived summary plus radar evidence, a title-free municipality comment, and expandable culture/history cards.
Historical place-name pins were removed from runtime data because the early-modern village polygons provide the intended village context.
Bakumatsu village polygons are approximate areas reconstructed from 2015 agricultural settlement boundaries.
Industrial heritage map pins were removed; 473 names across 242 municipalities remain in tourism/history landmark cards after merging names already present as tourism landmarks.
Runtime municipality GeoJSON keeps only the properties used by the app: layer_id, name, address, source, and subarea_name.

Cafe/restaurant runtime data excludes facility cafeterias, dorms, hospitals, kitchens, care facilities, schools, universities, companies, and factory-related entries by name/address keyword filtering.

Runtime municipality GeoJSON excludes facility names associated with schools, childcare, special-support schools, elder care, medical facilities, and universities. The app repeats the same check at load time and recalculates displayed layer counts and totals.
Runtime municipality GeoJSON also excludes disability facilities. Same-name public/cultural Point features inside one municipality are consolidated at their coordinate centroid.
All 1,145 P35-18 roadside stations are included in public_facilities.
Cafe/restaurant names that look like personal operator names are displayed as generic restaurant candidates in popups.
Large point-heavy municipalities render representative points on the map while result counts continue to use layer_counts and total_features.

The app uses data/story_asset_rules.json plus display_comment and feature names to show WebP illustrations during the fortune animation and behind the open result dialog; closing the dialog hides them.
The category side panel scrolls vertically on short screens, and the GSI tile attribution is always expanded.
Popups use a fixed bottom anchor so their cards stay above pins; early-modern village polygons have white boundary lines.
Clicking the map identifies a municipality by data/boundary_index.json plus the candidate boundary GeoJSON, then enables the clicked-city fortune button.
The side panel includes an in-app manual dialog explaining operations, data counts, restaurant data filtering, and caveats.
Do not load old nationwide layer GeoJSON files in the GitHub Pages app.
